register_platform.title: Register new access
register_platform.description: Both values come from the platform issuing your machines' tokens. Speakeasy trims surrounding spaces and otherwise stores them exactly as entered, because an assertion is matched against the spelling you register.

blocks.label: Name
blocks.help: How this issuer is labeled here. Not used for matching.

blocks.label: Description
blocks.placeholder: Claude agents in our Slack workspace
blocks.help: Optional. What this platform is and what runs on it, shown in place of the issuer URL in the Access Hub.

blocks.label: Issuer
blocks.help: The value an assertion's `iss` claim must carry. An https URL on a fully qualified domain, with no query or fragment.

blocks.label: JWKS URI
blocks.help: Where the issuer publishes its signing keys. This is the only field Speakeasy reads when verifying an assertion.

blocks.label: Tags
blocks.help: Optional labels for grouping platforms here. Not used for matching.

edit_platform.title: Edit platform
edit_platform.description: The issuer URL is fixed once a platform is registered. Changing the JWKS URI changes which keys Speakeasy accepts assertions from.

blocks.help: How this issuer is labeled here. Not used for matching.

blocks.label: Description
blocks.placeholder: Claude agents in our Slack workspace
blocks.help: Optional. What this platform is and what runs on it, shown in place of the issuer URL in the Access Hub.

blocks.label: Issuer
blocks.help: Fixed at registration. To trust a different issuer, register it as a new platform.

blocks.label: JWKS URI
blocks.help: Where the issuer publishes its signing keys. This is the only field Speakeasy reads when verifying an assertion.

blocks.label: Tags

allow_access.title: Allow access
allow_access.description: Allowing access lets a machine sign in to Speakeasy. The agent you choose supplies the whole policy that the machine acts under, so it is chosen at the same time.

blocks.label: Subject
blocks.help: Surrounding spaces are trimmed; otherwise stored and compared exactly as entered. End it with `*` to admit every subject beginning with the part before the `*`.

blocks.label: Agent
blocks.help: Choose the most narrowly scoped agent that can do the job. The machine inherits its policy in full.

blocks.label: Label (optional)
blocks.help: Useful where a subject is opaque, such as a numeric service account id.

blocks.label: Tags
blocks.help: Optional labels for finding this machine later. Not used for matching.

edit_access.title: Edit access
edit_access.description: The subject is fixed once access is allowed. Changing the agent changes the whole policy this machine acts under.

blocks.label: Subject
blocks.help: Fixed once access is allowed. To allow a different subject, allow access for it separately.

blocks.label: Agent
blocks.help: The machine inherits this agent's policy in full. Where the same subject is also allowed at the other tier, that access uses the same agent and changes with it.

blocks.label: Label (optional)
blocks.help: Useful where a subject is opaque, such as a numeric service account id.

blocks.label: Tags
blocks.help: Optional labels for finding this machine later. Not used for matching.
